He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Rhode Island Rams men's basketball|Rhode Island Rams]]. ==High school career== Terrell began his high school career at [[Weymouth High School]], where he averaged 11 points a game. He made big strides as a sophomore and posted 16 points per game and helped Weymouth to a [[Bay State Conference]] Carey Division title with an 18–4 record. The next season, Terrell transferred to the [[New Hampton School]], where one of his teammates was future NBA player [[Noah Vonleh]]. His time at New Hampton was marred by injuries and he transferred again to [[Brewster Academy]], where he was teammates with [[Devonte' Graham]]. During two years at Brewster, Terrell averaged 14.5 points, 5.0 rebounds and 3.0 assists. He guided the team to a New England prep title in 2013 and 2014 and was named the MVP of the tournament. Terrell led Brewster to their third National Prep Championship in 2014. Terrell formed a formidable backcourt at Brewster, which consisted of two other future NBA players in Devonte' Graham and [[Donovan Mitchell]]. Terrell was highly recruited out of high school and accepted a scholarship to [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]] before changing his mind and picking [[Rhode Island Rams men's basketball|Rhode Island]].{{cite news |last=Nazzaro |first=Adam |title=Weymouth's Terrell embraced March Madness |url=http://www.patriotledger.com/sports/20180402/weymouths-terrell-embraced-march-madness |access-date=June 2, 2018 |work=[[The Patriot Ledger]] |date=April 2, 2018 |archive-date=December 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181206054749/http://www.patriotledger.com/sports/20180402/weymouths-terrell-embraced-march-madness |url-status=dead }} ==College career== Despite posting four consecutive losing seasons before Terrell arrived, the Rams finished 23–10 his freshman year and reached the NIT. He was named to the All-Atlantic 10 Rookie Team.{{Cite web|url=http://www.atlantic10.com/pdf9/3272408.pdf|title=2014-15 Atlantic 10 Men's Basketball Awards|work=Atlantic10.com|access-date=June 2, 2018}} As a sophomore, he averaged 13.6 points per game on a 17–15 team. Terrell's scoring went down somewhat as a junior to 12.6 points per game, but the Rams finished 25–10 and reached the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. On November 27, 2017, Terrell had a career-high 32 points in a 75–74 win over [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]] and hit the game-winning layup with 5.2 seconds left.{{cite news |title=Terrell lifts Rhode Island past No. 20 Seton Hall, 75-74 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400988495 |access-date=June 2, 2018 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 23, 2017}} As a senior, he led Rhode Island in scoring with 16.8 points per game. He was named to the First Team All-Atlantic 10 as a senior.{{Cite news |date=March 6, 2018 |title=Aldridge, Adams Named Atlantic 10 Co-Players of the Year, Rhode Island's Hurley Voted as Coach of the Year |url=https://atlantic10.com/news/2018/3/6/211704410.aspx |access-date=January 2, 2025 |work=Atlantic10.com}} Terrell led the Rams to 26–8 record and an [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] appearance, where they beat [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]] behind 13 points from Terrell. Rhode Island bowed out in the second round to [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] with Terrell contributing 10 points. ==Professional career== Terrell went undrafted in the [[2018 NBA draft]] but was signed by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] to a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Iowa Wolves]] of the [[G League]] shortly thereafter.{{cite news |last=Frederick |first=Jace |title=Report: Timberwolves agree to two-way contract with Rhode Island's Jared Terrell |url=https://www.twincities.com/2018/06/22/report-timberwolves-agree-to-two-way-contract-with-rhode-islands-jared-terrell/ |access-date=June 24, 2018 |work=[[St. Paul Pioneer Press]] |date=June 22, 2018}} Terrell made his NBA debut on November 4, 2018, against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], playing 21 minutes and scoring four points off 1-of-8 shooting in a 111–81 loss.{{cite web|url=http://www.providencejournal.com/sports/20181106/rams-journal-coaches-debuts-start-new-eras-at-each-school|title=Rams Journal: Coaches' debuts start new eras at each school|first=Eric|last=Reub|work=[[The Providence Journal]]|date=November 6, 2018|access-date=December 5, 2018}} On September 14, 2019, Terrell signed a one-year deal with [[Hapoel Eilat B.C.|Hapoel Eilat]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]].{{cite news | title=ג'ארד טרל השלים את הסגל של אילת | url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=22550 | date=September 14, 2019 | work=basket.co.il | access-date=September 14, 2019 | language=he}} On October 28, 2019, Terrell recorded a season-high 25 points, while shooting 8-of-15 from the field, along with four rebounds in an 87–76 win over [[Maccabi Haifa B.C.|Maccabi Haifa]].{{cite news | title=Winner League, Game 4: Hapoel Yossi Avrahami Eilat Vs M. Haifa | url=http://basket.co.il/game-zone.asp?GameId=24043&lang=en | date=October 28, 2019 | work=basket.co.il | access-date=December 20, 2019}} On December 20, 2019, he parted ways with Eilat after appearing in six games due to an injury.{{cite news | title=בשל פציעה חוזרת: אילת שיחררה את ג'ארד טרל | url=https://www.one.co.il/Article/349930.html | date=December 20, 2019 | work=ONE.co.il |
